note: Generated. Do not hand-edit: run `go run ./cmd/provenance -write` from apps/common.
The compliance half of the release record. container/release-manifest.json is
the other half, and it is a separate file because it records what a
two-architecture Docker build produced and nothing else: adding a field to it
that no build produces would need either a rebuild to change one string, or a
no-build write path into the file that carries the build record, and the second
is a hole in exactly the guard #174 put there.
releaseManifest.sha256 is what stops the two halves drifting. Regenerating the
manifest without regenerating this bundle changes that digest and
TestProvenanceBundleIsTiedToTheReleaseManifest goes red.

unbuiltTargets.reason: the shipped artifact is a .spk, assembled by apps/synology/cmd/spkctl at release time rather than checked in; #85 owns building it and re-deriving each embedded binary's SHA-256 out of the finished package against container/release-manifest.json

the shipped artifact is a .upk, packed by ugcli against a known canonical image digest; that build is EPIC D's #83 and its App Center submission is #178, neither of which happens in this repository's gate

links.reason: the source repository is private, so every link into it is a 404 for a reviewer outside the project. The materials exist and are checked for substance on every run; what is missing is public access to them, which only the repository owner can grant. docs/compliance/source-offer.md is the written offer that stands until then.
